simple.meaning: אֲזָא (ʼăzâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to kindle ; (by implication) to heat.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:19. The surrounding contexts include death, commandment, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲזָא (H228) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֲזָא (ʼăzâʼ) / H228 is traced through Daniel 3:19, Daniel 3:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H228. aza [ אֲזָא ] verb make hot, heat ( ᵑ7 id . [rare]; compare Arabic kindle, burn ); — Pe`al Infinitive לְמֵזֵא (§ 11, 3 b)) Dan 3:19 ( ל accusative), suffix לְמֵזְיֵהּ 3:19 ; Passive participle אֵוֵה (K § 15 e ) 3:22 .

occurrences.englishText: Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated.

Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated.
Therefore because the king’s commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
